Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.
[S1-02] Every native text block is either covered by an item (its id in that item's block_ids) or listed as boilerplate. Boilerplate is only running headers, page numbers, publisher adverts, contact lines and watermarks; nothing teachable is boilerplate.
[S1-03] Every table becomes one 'table' item plus one 'table_row' item per row, in order, each row's content giving every cell with its column header, for example 'Smooth muscle | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary'. A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.
[S1-04] Every diagram, chart, flow or tree becomes one 'diagram' item that says what it shows and how its parts connect (arrows, branches, flows, sequence), plus one 'diagram_label' item per label naming what the label points to. A classification tree lists every branch and leaf with its parent.
[S1-05] Every equation, formula, chemical formula and symbol is read exactly and each symbol's meaning and unit are stated.
[S1-06] Understand every teachable item by questioning it like a teacher. Ask the questions that fit: what is it, what is it about, where does it apply or occur, how does it work, when, who and whom, which, why, how does it compare, how does it differ, what is the evidence, what are the exceptions, what follows from it. Then keep asking 'why' and 'how' on your own answers (depth 2, 3 ...) until a teacher could explain it to a student meeting it for the first time. Answers explain; they never just repeat the item's words.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-08] Give every item its true content type, one of BIE's nine: process, structure, classification, comparison, timeline, cause_effect, facts_numbers, figure, definition (bie/brain/rulebook/content_types.json). An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a question or an answer option is a role, not a type. BIE's code proposes a type before you read the page; when you choose another, say why. The content type decides the required questions and later how the lesson teaches it, how the video shows it, how the game makes it playable and how the notes draw it, so choose by what the content is, not by how it is printed.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.
- text_image_disagreements: where the text layer and the image differ.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

items.content: 3. Sclerenchyma Tissue
items.exam_note: Major permanent-tissue identification topic.

items.content:
Occurrence:
• In stems around vascular bundles.
• In veins of leaves.
• Hard covering of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: What distribution of sclerenchyma does the page describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs around stem vascular bundles, in leaf veins and in the hard coverings of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: Where should a learner look for the stem and leaf examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Look around the conducting bundles inside a stem and along the vein framework of a leaf.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is strengthening tissue useful at these sites?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stems and leaf veins need resistance to bending, while seed and nut coverings need resistance to physical damage.

prerequisites: vascular bundle as a group of conducting tissues
items.exam_note: Location-based matching and correct-statement questions.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में पानी और भोजन ले जाने वाले tissues के गुच्छे
terms.everyday_image: एक साथ बँधी पानी की पाइपें

why_chain.step: Stems, veins and coverings face bending or physical damage.
Sclerenchyma provides mechanical strength and protection at such sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace a familiar leaf's veins, then zoom into supporting tissue.
unpack.consequence: Location can help identify the tissue's support role.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue around vascular bundles from the conducting bundle itself.

items.content: Eg. Husk of coconut.

teacher_understanding.question: What familiar example identifies sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page gives coconut husk as its example.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the husk on a coconut?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the fibrous outer covering outside the hard shell.

teacher_understanding.question: How does handling coconut husk help explain this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its tough fibres resist pulling apart, giving an everyday experience of mechanical strength.

items.exam_note: Classic tissue–example match; distinguish husk from shell.

terms.plain_meaning: नारियल के बाहर का रेशेदार हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: नारियल से खींचकर अलग किए जाने वाले भूरे रेशे

why_chain.step: A coconut needs a protective outer covering.
Tough sclerenchyma fibres provide a familiar example of protective strength.

unpack.consequence: A daily-life object anchors sclerenchyma identification.
unpack.level_extra: Remember the printed example precisely.

items.content:
Structure:
➢ Long and narrow
➢ Walls are thickened by LIGNINS

teacher_understanding.question: What shape and wall property does the book assign to sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cells are described as long and narrow, with walls thickened by lignins.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the strengthening material deposited?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin is deposited in the cell wall rather than being a filling between neighbouring cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does lignification help support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin makes walls rigid and resistant to deformation, allowing them to bear mechanical stress.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the long-and-narrow description cover all sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: It particularly describes fibres. Sclereids are another sclerenchyma form and can have other shapes.

items.exam_note: Lignified wall is a key identifying feature; avoid generalising fibre shape to all forms.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबाई ज़्यादा, चौड़ाई कम
terms.everyday_image: पतली लंबी डोरी

terms.plain_meaning: cell wall को कड़ा बनाने वाला पदार्थ
terms.everyday_image: दीवार को मज़बूत करने वाला अतिरिक्त भराव

why_chain.step: A plant needs walls that resist bending and compression.
Lignin reinforces those walls, producing rigid support.

unpack.consequence: Thick walls explain strength better than memorising the tissue name alone.
unpack.level_extra: Know lignin as the wall-strengthening material; recognise the fibre-shape qualification.

items.content: ➢ Cell cavity is absent due to excessive thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page say the cell cavity is absent?
teacher_understanding.answer: It attributes the absence to excessive wall thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this be understood accurately?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall deposition reduces the internal space, called the lumen. In sclerenchyma the lumen is commonly narrow, not necessarily completely absent.

items.exam_note: Distinguish thick wall and reduced lumen from a universal absence of lumen.

terms.plain_meaning: cell wall के भीतर की जगह
terms.everyday_image: मोटी दीवार वाले पाइप का छोटा अंदरूनी रास्ता

why_chain.step: Support requires a strongly reinforced wall.
Increasing wall thickness reduces the internal cavity; complete absence is not universal.

unpack.example_or_place: A cross-section through a sclerenchyma fibre.
unpack.consequence: Keep the inside-cell lumen distinct from spaces between cells.
unpack.level_extra: The printed absolute is qualified rather than silently adopted.

items.content:
➢ Intercellular spaces absent.
➢ Cells are dead.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement and living status are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes cells without intercellular spaces and identifies the cells as dead.

teacher_understanding.question: Where would an intercellular space be, unlike a cell cavity?
teacher_understanding.answer: It would lie between neighbouring cells; a cell cavity lies inside one cell's wall.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells still provide support?
teacher_understanding.answer: At maturity, the protoplasm is lost but the thick walls remain, so physical reinforcement does not require a living cell interior.

items.exam_note: Dead at maturity versus living support tissues is a common comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास के cells के बीच की खाली जगह
terms.everyday_image: जुड़ी ईंटों के बीच बचा गैप

why_chain.step: A support framework must remain mechanically firm.
Closely arranged thick walls can provide support after the living contents are lost.

unpack.consequence: Dead does not mean functionless.
unpack.level_extra: Separate cell cavity, intercellular space and living status in statement questions.

items.content:
Function:
• Provide strength to plant cell.
• Provides protection and mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: Why is sclerenchyma useful to a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides strength, protection and mechanical strength.

teacher_understanding.question: How do its structural features produce these benefits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Rigid lignified walls form a reinforcing framework that resists deformation and helps protect enclosed parts.

items.exam_note: Match structure with function; do not confuse support with food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: दबाव, खिंचाव या मुड़ने पर टूटने से बचने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मज़बूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: Plant parts experience forces that could bend or damage them.
Sclerenchyma supplies a rigid protective framework.

unpack.example_or_place: Hard seed coverings and coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: Location, thick walls and protective function form one explanation.
unpack.level_extra: Use a location–structure–function chain for correct-statement questions.

items.content: COMPLEX PERMANENT TISSUE
items.exam_note: Introduces vascular tissues.

items.content:
• Made up of more than one type of cells.
• Cells co-ordinate to perform common function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes this tissue complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different cell types form one tissue and coordinate for a common function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is this organisation illustrated on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The xylem and phloem drawings show several labelled components within each tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can several cell types be useful in one tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A transport system needs conducting routes as well as support and associated living cells, so different cells can divide the work.

items.exam_note: Complex means multiple cell types, not merely a large number of cells.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम करके एक साझा काम पूरा करना
terms.everyday_image: रसोई में कोई काटता है, कोई पकाता है, खाना मिलकर बनता है

why_chain.step: Transport needs more than an unsupported passage.
Different cell types work together as a complex tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem combines conducting cells, parenchyma and fibres.
unpack.consequence: This prepares the learner to recognise components rather than treat xylem as one cell.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast with simple permanent tissue using cell-type diversity as the criterion.

items.content:
Functions:
• Transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need transport tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and minerals are obtained mainly through roots, whereas food is made mainly in leaves; other parts need supplies from these sources.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe the contribution of complex tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: They transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this transport divided between the two named tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly transports water and minerals; phloem transports food substances.

items.exam_note: Do not assign all three transported materials equally to each tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: ज़रूरी चीज़ों को एक हिस्से से दूसरे तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: घर में टंकी से अलग-अलग नलों तक पानी पहुँचना

why_chain.step: Places of supply and places of use are separated in a plant.
Complex tissues move water, minerals and food between plant parts.

unpack.example_or_place: Roots, stem and leaves linked by conducting tissues.
unpack.consequence: Different transport roles lead to xylem–phloem comparison.
unpack.level_extra: Know the cargo associated with each tissue.

items.content:
Two types:
1. Xylem
2. Phloem

teacher_understanding.question: Which two complex permanent tissues are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and phloem are the two types listed.

teacher_understanding.question: What main functional difference separates them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and minerals, while phloem carries food substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both still in the same broad group?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each contains different cell types coordinating in transport, which is the basis of complex-tissue organisation.

items.exam_note: Classify xylem and phloem as complex permanent tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्यतः पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी पहुँचाने वाली पाइप-व्यवस्था

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना भोजन पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: तैयार खाना अलग-अलग जगह पहुँचाने वाली व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Plants need water supplies and distribution of food.
Xylem and phloem specialise in these different transport roles.

unpack.example_or_place: The paired diagrams on this page.
unpack.consequence: Both are complex tissues but are not interchangeable.
unpack.level_extra: Use the hierarchy: permanent tissue → complex → xylem/phloem.

items.content: Complex Permanent Tissue: paired labelled drawings of Xylem and Phloem. Xylem shows elongated conducting and supporting elements with surrounding parenchyma. Phloem shows stacked sieve-tube regions, adjacent companion cells, fibres and parenchyma. Leader arrows identify parts; they do not indicate transport direction.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the paired figure demonstrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each named complex tissue consists of several different components, not one uniform cell type.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues are shown side by side?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is on the left and phloem on the right.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the arrows be read?
teacher_understanding.answer: Follow each leader from a component to its name; these are identification arrows rather than a diagram of flow.

items.exam_note: Component identification and odd-one-out questions.

why_chain.step: A complex tissue must contain different cell types.
The labels reveal the different parts within each tissue.

unpack.consequence: A component must be matched to the correct tissue.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret leader arrows as movement arrows.

items.content: Xylem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The parenchyma component of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions does the page attach to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food storage and sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this expand the idea of a water-conducting tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem includes storage and lateral-transfer cells alongside the main conducting elements.

items.exam_note: A xylem component with storage and lateral-conduction roles.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem में भोजन जमा करने और पानी बगल में पहुँचाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य पाइप के पास छोटा भंडार और बगल का रास्ता

unpack.consequence: Xylem is more than hollow conduits.
unpack.level_extra: Connect label to storage and sideways conduction.

items.content: Vessels — leader identifies the broad conducting element in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled Vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: A conducting component of the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other component shares its conducting role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids also transport water and minerals.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the vessel suited to conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its tubular structure provides a route for vertical water and mineral transport.

items.exam_note: Plant vessels here are not blood vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem के पानी ले जाने वाले नली जैसे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: जुड़े पाइपों का रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: Broad element in the xylem figure.
unpack.consequence: Links tube shape to transport.
unpack.level_extra: Match vessels with xylem.

items.content: Tracheids — leader identifies the elongated conducting elements of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Tracheids name?
teacher_understanding.answer: One of the four components listed for xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which transport role is associated with them?
teacher_understanding.answer: They conduct water and minerals vertically, together with vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their shape support the role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their elongated tubular form supplies a route along the plant.

items.exam_note: Tracheids belong to xylem, not phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाले लंबे xylem cells
terms.everyday_image: लंबी पतली नलियों की कतार

unpack.consequence: Two kinds of conducting elements must be recognised.
unpack.level_extra: Pair tracheids with vessels for conduction.

items.content: Xylem Fibres — leader identifies the supporting fibres in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The fibre component within xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which principal function belongs to these fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their function is mainly supportive.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are fibres useful beside conduits?
teacher_understanding.answer: They reinforce the tissue and help it resist mechanical forces.

items.exam_note: Do not assign the main conducting role to xylem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem को सहारा देने वाले लंबे मज़बूत cells
terms.everyday_image: पाइप के साथ लगा सहारा

unpack.consequence: Support is part of complex-tissue teamwork.
unpack.level_extra: Support versus conduction is the key distinction.

items.content: Phloem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the phloem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What component is named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma belonging to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains this labelled component?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand tissue, phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does phloem parenchyma contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: These living cells help store food and participate in lateral movement of food substances.

items.exam_note: Parenchyma occurs in both named complex tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem में भोजन सँभालने वाले living cells
terms.everyday_image: डिलीवरी रास्ते के पास छोटा भंडार

unpack.consequence: The word parenchyma alone does not identify xylem exclusively.
unpack.level_extra: Use the xylem/phloem qualifier.

items.content: Companion cell — leader identifies the slender cell beside a sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled beside the sieve tube?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue should be associated with companion cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem, as shown in the right-hand illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this neighbouring cell important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supports sieve-tube function through close metabolic cooperation and helps in loading and unloading sugars.

items.exam_note: Companion cell is a diagnostic phloem label.

terms.plain_meaning: sieve tube के पास रहकर उसका काम सँभालने वाला cell
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य काम करने वाले के पास उसका सहायक

unpack.example_or_place: Beside the sieve tube in phloem.
unpack.consequence: Transport cells work with neighbouring cells.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise the sieve tube–companion cell association.

items.content: Phloem fibres — leader identifies the elongated supporting component in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What part does this label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres within the phloem tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other illustrated tissue also contains fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem also has labelled fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: How do phloem fibres contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick walls provide mechanical support rather than acting as the main food-conducting route.

items.exam_note: Fibres are not exclusive to xylem.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem को मज़बूती देने वाले रेशे जैसे cells
terms.everyday_image: नली के साथ बँधी मज़बूत डोरी

unpack.consequence: Supporting cells coexist with food-conducting cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish fibres from sieve tubes.

items.content: Sieve tube — leader identifies the main elongated tube in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What main phloem structure is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neighbouring cell is also labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell lies beside it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a sieve tube serve transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve-tube elements join end to end, with perforated end regions allowing movement of food-containing sap.

items.exam_note: Sieve tube belongs to phloem, unlike vessels and tracheids.

terms.plain_meaning: भोजन वाला रस ले जाने वाली phloem की नली
terms.everyday_image: बीच-बीच में छन्नी जैसे जोड़ वाला पाइप

unpack.example_or_place: Large phloem tube in the right illustration.
unpack.consequence: The lower figure explains its component cells and end plates.
unpack.level_extra: Match sieve tube with food transport.

items.content: Xylem structure / Phloem structure. The xylem side shows an isolated vessel element with pitted walls (a), tracheids, and a grouped view (b) labelled xylem parenchyma cell, vessel element, pitted walls and tracheid. The phloem side shows an isolated sieve-tube element with sieve plate, companion cell, nucleus and phloem parenchyma cells, alongside a grouped view (b) labelled companion cell, sieve-tube element, sieve plate, phloem parenchyma cells and plasmo-desmata [plasmodesmata]. Leader lines identify structures rather than flow directions.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra detail does the boxed figure add?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows individual elements and grouped arrangements, including pitted xylem walls and the sieve plates and associated cells of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parts connect the figure to transport pathways?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements and tracheids are shown on the xylem side; sieve-tube elements and sieve plates on the phloem side.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these details improve understanding beyond a tissue name?
teacher_understanding.answer: They distinguish the tube-forming cells from the neighbouring support and storage cells, and show specialised regions through which exchange or continuity occurs.

items.exam_note: Recognise pits versus sieve plates and individual elements versus whole tubes.

why_chain.step: A transport route needs continuity along its length and connections with nearby cells.
The detailed views reveal wall pits, sieve plates and cell connections.

unpack.consequence: Transport tissue is an organised assembly, not a featureless pipe.
unpack.level_extra: Panel letters a and b mark views, not biological structures.

items.where_on_page: boxed figure, far-left isolated xylem cell
items.content: vessel elements — leader points to the isolated elongated pink vessel element.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the isolated pink structure?
teacher_understanding.answer: A vessel element, identified by the label vessel elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an element differ from the whole vessel?
teacher_understanding.answer: An element is one constituent cell; vessel elements connect end to end to form a vessel.

items.exam_note: Element versus entire vessel.

terms.plain_meaning: मिलकर vessel बनाने वाले अलग-अलग cells
terms.everyday_image: लंबी पाइप बनाने वाले छोटे पाइप के टुकड़े

unpack.consequence: One cell need not equal the entire conduit.
unpack.level_extra: Read element as a building unit.

items.where_on_page: boxed figure, beside isolated vessel element
items.content: pitted walls — leader points to pits in the isolated vessel element's wall.

teacher_understanding.question: What wall feature is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pitted walls on the isolated vessel element.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue's conducting element shows these pits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do pits help conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are regions where secondary wall thickening is absent, facilitating water movement between adjacent cells through the remaining pit membranes.

items.exam_note: Pits are wall regions, not sieve plates.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी wall में कम मोटाई वाले छोटे-छोटे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: मोटी दीवार में पतली खिड़की जैसी जगहें

unpack.consequence: A thick wall can still allow lateral exchange.
unpack.level_extra: Do not imagine every pit as a completely empty hole.

items.content: tracheids — leader points to the narrow, tapered pink cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What cells are labelled tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: The elongated tapered cells shown between the isolated vessel and grouped xylem view.

teacher_understanding.question: Which listed tissue component do they represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tracheid component of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does water move between adjoining tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: It passes through pit regions in their overlapping walls.

items.exam_note: Recognise tapering tracheids.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरों पर पतले होते लंबे पानी ले जाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: पास-पास रखी नुकीले सिरों वाली पतली नलियाँ

unpack.example_or_place: Narrow pink cells in the boxed xylem figure.
unpack.consequence: Their form differs from broad vessel elements.
unpack.level_extra: Use shape alongside the label, not colour alone.

items.where_on_page: boxed figure, top of grouped xylem
items.content: xylem parenchyma cell — leader points to the slender grey cell beside the pink vessel elements.

teacher_understanding.question: What is identified beside the vessel?
teacher_understanding.answer: A xylem parenchyma cell.

teacher_understanding.question: Which page functions belong to this cell type?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food storage and sideways water conduction.

teacher_understanding.question: Why show it beside conducting elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: That arrangement illustrates how lateral-transfer and storage cells belong to the same complex tissue as the main conduits.

items.exam_note: Identify the non-conduit component.

unpack.example_or_place: Grey cell beside grouped pink xylem elements.

teacher_understanding.question: How can pits reconcile strength with exchange?
teacher_understanding.answer: Most of the secondary wall is reinforced, while pit regions permit water exchange through thinner wall regions.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue does it belong to?

teacher_understanding.question: How should this label be used despite the unclear pointer?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use it to identify the named xylem component, but do not infer a precise pointed cell from the unclear leader.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a sieve plate permit continuity?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its pores allow sap to move between adjoining sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.answer: A sieve tube in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How are successive elements linked?
teacher_understanding.answer: They meet end to end at sieve plates, permitting movement of sap.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell is it shown accompanying?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sieve-tube element.

teacher_understanding.answer: The companion cell retains a nucleus; the mature sieve-tube element lacks one.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help explain their cooperation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The nucleated companion cell supports the metabolic needs of the associated sieve-tube element.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के काम का नियंत्रण और आनुवंशिक जानकारी रखने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: काम सँभालने वाला नियंत्रण कक्ष

teacher_understanding.answer: They are associated living storage and lateral-transfer cells rather than the main longitudinal food-conducting elements.

items.exam_note: Identify phloem's associated cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which structure separates successive elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing labels a sieve plate at their junction.

teacher_understanding.question: How do elements contribute to a long-distance route?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their end-to-end arrangement forms a sieve tube through which food-containing sap moves.

items.exam_note: Identify the main conducting cell rather than its neighbour.

unpack.consequence: A longitudinal route is assembled from several cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish element, tube and plate.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this transverse label identify?

teacher_understanding.answer: The isolated sieve-tube element to the left.

teacher_understanding.answer: Its pores allow sap to pass across the junction instead of creating a completely sealed barrier.

items.content: phloem parenchyma cells — leader points to cells beside the grouped sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other phloem cell types appear alongside them?
teacher_understanding.answer: The drawing labels companion cells and sieve-tube elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why retain a separate label for parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Associated storage cells and companion cells have different roles, even though both occur next to conducting elements.

items.exam_note: Do not merge all associated cells into companion cells.

unpack.consequence: Makes cell-type diversity visible.

teacher_understanding.question: What fine connections are labelled?

teacher_understanding.question: Which kind of connection does the term refer to?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cytoplasmic channels across cell walls between neighbouring living plant cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these connections help coordinated function?
teacher_understanding.answer: They allow substances and signals to move directly between adjacent living cells.

items.content: • Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: What four components make up xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Where can these components be identified on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: All four are named in the upper xylem diagram; the lower illustration enlarges conducting elements and parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How are their jobs divided according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids and vessels conduct water and minerals, parenchyma stores food and conducts water sideways, and fibres mainly support.

items.exam_note: Four-component list is central to matching and odd-one-out questions.

terms.plain_meaning: इन अलग-अलग हिस्सों से मिलकर बना है
terms.everyday_image: एक टीम में अलग काम वाले सदस्य

why_chain.step: A functioning transport tissue needs conduits, storage and reinforcement.
Xylem divides these roles among its four components.

unpack.consequence: Xylem is a tissue, not the name of one cell type.
unpack.level_extra: Companion cells and sieve tubes are phloem distractors.

items.content: • Tracheids and vessels have thick walls, and many are dead cells when mature.

teacher_understanding.question: What mature features of the conducting elements are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: They have thick walls, and the page says many are dead when mature.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are these thick-walled elements located?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are conducting components of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are thick walls and loss of living contents useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thick lignified walls resist collapse, while loss of the protoplast leaves a low-resistance pathway for water movement.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this mean the whole of xylem is dead?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Xylem parenchyma is living; the conventional description of mature tracheids and vessel elements is that they are dead.

items.exam_note: Avoid 'all xylem cells are dead'; preserve the page's word 'many'.

terms.plain_meaning: अपना पूरा आकार और खास काम करने की अवस्था में पहुँचा हुआ
terms.everyday_image: बनकर इस्तेमाल के लिए तैयार पाइप

why_chain.step: Water pathways must remain open and resist collapse.
Strong walls and an empty mature interior support this conducting role.

unpack.example_or_place: Mature xylem tracheids and vessel elements.
unpack.consequence: Conducting dead cells can coexist with living parenchyma in one tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: clear the interior, retain the wall
unpack.level_extra: Differentiate component-level statements from whole-tissue statements.

items.content: • Tracheids and vessels are tubular structures. This allows them to transport water and minerals vertically.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page connect tubular form with conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tube-like structure allows water and minerals to be transported vertically.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these cells form a route through a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements join end to end, while overlapping tracheids transfer water through pits, producing connected longitudinal pathways.

teacher_understanding.question: Does tube shape alone explain why water rises?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Tube shape provides the route; transpiration pull and the cohesion of water are major contributors to upward movement.

items.exam_note: Relate shape to vertical conduction; do not equate the route with the driving force.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे की लंबाई की दिशा में, ऊपर की ओर जाने वाला रास्ता
terms.everyday_image: ज़मीन से ऊपर की मंज़िल तक जाती पानी की पाइप

why_chain.step: Water absorbed below must reach leaves above.
Tubular xylem elements provide longitudinal water-and-mineral pathways.

unpack.example_or_place: From root through stem toward leaves.
unpack.consequence: Vertical conduction contrasts with the sideways movement described next.
unpack.level_extra: This is structure–function reasoning, not a complete mechanism of ascent of sap.

items.content: • The parenchyma stores food and help [helps] in sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does xylem need more than vertical conducting elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water must also be distributed laterally to neighbouring tissues, and stored food can support local needs.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem parenchyma contribute according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: It stores food and helps in sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from tracheids and vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their stated role is vertical transport of water and minerals, whereas parenchyma adds storage and sideways water movement.

items.exam_note: Food storage in xylem is not the same as phloem's long-distance food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी को बगल के हिस्सों तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य पाइप से बगल के कमरे में जाती शाखा

why_chain.step: A main upward route alone does not supply all neighbouring cells.
Parenchyma helps sideways conduction and also stores food.

unpack.consequence: Water distribution has both longitudinal and lateral components.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the trap that any mention of food makes a cell part of phloem.

items.content: • Xylem fibres are mainly supportive in function.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are supportive fibres useful in xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tissue must withstand mechanical stresses while maintaining its conducting framework.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page distinguish the fibre role?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies fibres as mainly supportive, unlike the conducting role assigned to tracheids and vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres provide that support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick, lignified walls reinforce the tissue against deformation.

items.exam_note: Match fibres–support, parenchyma–storage/lateral conduction, tracheids and vessels–conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: ढाँचे को टिकाए रखने और मज़बूत बनाने वाला
terms.everyday_image: पानी की पाइप को थामे रखने वाला मज़बूत सहारा

why_chain.step: A transport framework must resist bending and damage.
Xylem fibres provide mainly mechanical support.

unpack.consequence: Completes the division of labour among the four xylem components.
unpack.level_extra: Retain 'mainly': the page states the principal role, not an absolute exclusion.

items.content: 3. Sclerenchyma Tissue
items.exam_note: Major permanent-tissue identification topic.

items.content:
Occurrence:
• In stems around vascular bundles.
• In veins of leaves.
• Hard covering of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: What distribution of sclerenchyma does the page describe?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs around stem vascular bundles, in leaf veins and in the hard coverings of seeds and nuts.

teacher_understanding.question: Where should a learner look for the stem and leaf examples?
teacher_understanding.answer: Look around the conducting bundles inside a stem and along the vein framework of a leaf.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is strengthening tissue useful at these sites?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stems and leaf veins need resistance to bending, while seed and nut coverings need resistance to physical damage.

items.exam_note: Location-based matching and correct-statement questions.

why_chain.step: Stems, veins and coverings face bending or physical damage.
Sclerenchyma provides mechanical strength and protection at such sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Trace a familiar leaf's veins, then zoom into supporting tissue.
unpack.consequence: Location can help identify the tissue's support role.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue around vascular bundles from the conducting bundle itself.

items.content: Eg. Husk of coconut.

teacher_understanding.question: What familiar example identifies sclerenchyma?

teacher_understanding.question: How does handling coconut husk help explain this tissue?

unpack.level_extra: The printed absolute is qualified rather than silently adopted.

items.content:
➢ Intercellular spaces absent.
➢ Cells are dead.

teacher_understanding.question: What arrangement and living status are stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes cells without intercellular spaces and identifies the cells as dead.

teacher_understanding.question: Where would an intercellular space be, unlike a cell cavity?
teacher_understanding.answer: It would lie between neighbouring cells; a cell cavity lies inside one cell's wall.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells still provide support?
teacher_understanding.answer: At maturity, the protoplasm is lost but the thick walls remain, so physical reinforcement does not require a living cell interior.

items.exam_note: Dead at maturity versus living support tissues is a common comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास के cells के बीच की खाली जगह
terms.everyday_image: जुड़ी ईंटों के बीच बचा गैप

why_chain.step: A support framework must remain mechanically firm.
Closely arranged thick walls can provide support after the living contents are lost.

unpack.consequence: Dead does not mean functionless.
unpack.level_extra: Separate cell cavity, intercellular space and living status in statement questions.

items.content:
Function:
• Provide strength to plant cell.
• Provides protection and mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: Why is sclerenchyma useful to a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides strength, protection and mechanical strength.

teacher_understanding.question: How do its structural features produce these benefits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Rigid lignified walls form a reinforcing framework that resists deformation and helps protect enclosed parts.

items.exam_note: Match structure with function; do not confuse support with food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: दबाव, खिंचाव या मुड़ने पर टूटने से बचने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मज़बूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: Plant parts experience forces that could bend or damage them.
Sclerenchyma supplies a rigid protective framework.

unpack.example_or_place: Hard seed coverings and coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: Location, thick walls and protective function form one explanation.
unpack.level_extra: Use a location–structure–function chain for correct-statement questions.

items.content: COMPLEX PERMANENT TISSUE
items.exam_note: Introduces vascular tissues.

items.content:
• Made up of more than one type of cells.
• Cells co-ordinate to perform common function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes this tissue complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different cell types form one tissue and coordinate for a common function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is this organisation illustrated on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The xylem and phloem drawings show several labelled components within each tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can several cell types be useful in one tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A transport system needs conducting routes as well as support and associated living cells, so different cells can divide the work.

items.exam_note: Complex means multiple cell types, not merely a large number of cells.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम करके एक साझा काम पूरा करना
terms.everyday_image: रसोई में कोई काटता है, कोई पकाता है, खाना मिलकर बनता है

why_chain.step: Transport needs more than an unsupported passage.
Different cell types work together as a complex tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Xylem combines conducting cells, parenchyma and fibres.
unpack.consequence: This prepares the learner to recognise components rather than treat xylem as one cell.
unpack.level_extra: Contrast with simple permanent tissue using cell-type diversity as the criterion.

items.content:
Functions:
• Transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need transport tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and minerals are obtained mainly through roots, whereas food is made mainly in leaves; other parts need supplies from these sources.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page describe the contribution of complex tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: They transport water, minerals and food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this transport divided between the two named tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly transports water and minerals; phloem transports food substances.

items.exam_note: Do not assign all three transported materials equally to each tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: ज़रूरी चीज़ों को एक हिस्से से दूसरे तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: घर में टंकी से अलग-अलग नलों तक पानी पहुँचना

why_chain.step: Places of supply and places of use are separated in a plant.
Complex tissues move water, minerals and food between plant parts.

unpack.example_or_place: Roots, stem and leaves linked by conducting tissues.
unpack.consequence: Different transport roles lead to xylem–phloem comparison.
unpack.level_extra: Know the cargo associated with each tissue.

items.content:
Two types:
1. Xylem
2. Phloem

teacher_understanding.question: Which two complex permanent tissues are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and phloem are the two types listed.

teacher_understanding.question: What main functional difference separates them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and minerals, while phloem carries food substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both still in the same broad group?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each contains different cell types coordinating in transport, which is the basis of complex-tissue organisation.

items.exam_note: Classify xylem and phloem as complex permanent tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्यतः पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी पहुँचाने वाली पाइप-व्यवस्था

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना भोजन पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: तैयार खाना अलग-अलग जगह पहुँचाने वाली व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Plants need water supplies and distribution of food.
Xylem and phloem specialise in these different transport roles.

unpack.example_or_place: The paired diagrams on this page.
unpack.consequence: Both are complex tissues but are not interchangeable.
unpack.level_extra: Use the hierarchy: permanent tissue → complex → xylem/phloem.

items.content: Complex Permanent Tissue: paired labelled drawings of Xylem and Phloem. Xylem shows elongated conducting and supporting elements with surrounding parenchyma. Phloem shows stacked sieve-tube regions, adjacent companion cells, fibres and parenchyma. Leader arrows identify parts; they do not indicate transport direction.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the paired figure demonstrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each named complex tissue consists of several different components, not one uniform cell type.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues are shown side by side?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is on the left and phloem on the right.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the arrows be read?
teacher_understanding.answer: Follow each leader from a component to its name; these are identification arrows rather than a diagram of flow.

items.exam_note: Component identification and odd-one-out questions.

why_chain.step: A complex tissue must contain different cell types.
The labels reveal the different parts within each tissue.

unpack.consequence: A component must be matched to the correct tissue.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret leader arrows as movement arrows.

items.content: Xylem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The parenchyma component of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions does the page attach to it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food storage and sideways conduction of water.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this expand the idea of a water-conducting tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem includes storage and lateral-transfer cells alongside the main conducting elements.

items.exam_note: A xylem component with storage and lateral-conduction roles.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem में भोजन जमा करने और पानी बगल में पहुँचाने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: मुख्य पाइप के पास छोटा भंडार और बगल का रास्ता

unpack.consequence: Xylem is more than hollow conduits.
unpack.level_extra: Connect label to storage and sideways conduction.

items.content: Vessels — leader identifies the broad conducting element in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled Vessels?
teacher_understanding.answer: A conducting component of the xylem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other component shares its conducting role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids also transport water and minerals.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the vessel suited to conduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its tubular structure provides a route for vertical water and mineral transport.

items.exam_note: Plant vessels here are not blood vessels.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem के पानी ले जाने वाले नली जैसे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: जुड़े पाइपों का रास्ता

unpack.example_or_place: Broad element in the xylem figure.
unpack.consequence: Links tube shape to transport.
unpack.level_extra: Match vessels with xylem.

items.content: Tracheids — leader identifies the elongated conducting elements of xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Tracheids name?
teacher_understanding.answer: One of the four components listed for xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which transport role is associated with them?
teacher_understanding.answer: They conduct water and minerals vertically, together with vessels.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their shape support the role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their elongated tubular form supplies a route along the plant.

items.exam_note: Tracheids belong to xylem, not phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाले लंबे xylem cells
terms.everyday_image: लंबी पतली नलियों की कतार

unpack.consequence: Two kinds of conducting elements must be recognised.
unpack.level_extra: Pair tracheids with vessels for conduction.

items.content: Xylem Fibres — leader identifies the supporting fibres in xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The fibre component within xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which principal function belongs to these fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their function is mainly supportive.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are fibres useful beside conduits?
teacher_understanding.answer: They reinforce the tissue and help it resist mechanical forces.

items.exam_note: Do not assign the main conducting role to xylem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem को सहारा देने वाले लंबे मज़बूत cells
terms.everyday_image: पाइप के साथ लगा सहारा

unpack.consequence: Support is part of complex-tissue teamwork.
unpack.level_extra: Support versus conduction is the key distinction.

items.content: Phloem Parenchyma — leader identifies parenchyma in the phloem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: What component is named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma belonging to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains this labelled component?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand tissue, phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does phloem parenchyma contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: These living cells help store food and participate in lateral movement of food substances.

items.exam_note: Parenchyma occurs in both named complex tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem में भोजन सँभालने वाले living cells
terms.everyday_image: डिलीवरी रास्ते के पास छोटा भंडार

unpack.consequence: The word parenchyma alone does not identify xylem exclusively.
unpack.level_extra: Use the xylem/phloem qualifier.

items.content: Companion cell — leader identifies the slender cell beside a sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: What is labelled beside the sieve tube?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue should be associated with companion cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem, as shown in the right-hand illustration.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this neighbouring cell important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supports sieve-tube function through close metabolic cooperation and helps in loading and unloading sugars.

items.exam_note: Companion cell is a diagnostic phloem label.

terms.everyday_image: मुख्य काम करने वाले के पास उसका सहायक

unpack.example_or_place: Beside the sieve tube in phloem.
unpack.consequence: Transport cells work with neighbouring cells.
unpack.level_extra: Recognise the sieve tube–companion cell association.

items.content: Phloem fibres — leader identifies the elongated supporting component in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What part does this label name?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres within the phloem tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other illustrated tissue also contains fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem also has labelled fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: How do phloem fibres contribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their thick walls provide mechanical support rather than acting as the main food-conducting route.

items.exam_note: Fibres are not exclusive to xylem.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem को मज़बूती देने वाले रेशे जैसे cells
terms.everyday_image: नली के साथ बँधी मज़बूत डोरी

unpack.consequence: Supporting cells coexist with food-conducting cells.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish fibres from sieve tubes.

items.content: Sieve tube — leader identifies the main elongated tube in phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What main phloem structure is labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sieve tube.

teacher_understanding.question: Which neighbouring cell is also labelled?
teacher_understanding.answer: A companion cell lies beside it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a sieve tube serve transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve-tube elements join end to end, with perforated end regions allowing movement of food-containing sap.

items.exam_note: Sieve tube belongs to phloem, unlike vessels and tracheids.

terms.plain_meaning: भोजन वाला रस ले जाने वाली phloem की नली
terms.everyday_image: बीच-बीच में छन्नी जैसे जोड़ वाला पाइप

unpack.example_or_place: Large phloem tube in the right illustration.
unpack.consequence: The lower figure explains its component cells and end plates.
unpack.level_extra: Match sieve tube with food transport.

items.content: Xylem structure / Phloem structure. The xylem side shows an isolated vessel element with pitted walls (a), tracheids, and a grouped view (b) labelled xylem parenchyma cell, vessel element, pitted walls and tracheid. The phloem side shows an isolated sieve-tube element with sieve plate, companion cell, nucleus and phloem parenchyma cells, alongside a grouped view (b) labelled companion cell, sieve-tube element, sieve plate, phloem parenchyma cells and plasmo-desmata [plasmodesmata]. Leader lines identify structures rather than flow directions.

teacher_understanding.question: What extra detail does the boxed figure add?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows individual elements and grouped arrangements, including pitted xylem walls and the sieve plates and associated cells of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parts connect the figure to transport pathways?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements and tracheids are shown on the xylem side; sieve-tube elements and sieve plates on the phloem side.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these details improve understanding beyond a tissue name?
teacher_understanding.answer: They distinguish the tube-forming cells from the neighbouring support and storage cells, and show specialised regions through which exchange or continuity occurs.

items.exam_note: Recognise pits versus sieve plates and individual elements versus whole tubes.

why_chain.step: A transport route needs continuity along its length and connections with nearby cells.
The detailed views reveal wall pits, sieve plates and cell connections.

unpack.consequence: Transport tissue is an organised assembly, not a featureless pipe.
unpack.level_extra: Panel letters a and b mark views, not biological structures.

teacher_understanding.answer: An element is one constituent cell; vessel elements connect end to end to form a vessel.
